biological.citation: Nora et al. 2017 - Targeted Degradation of CTCF Decouples Local Insulation of Chromosome Domains from Genomic Compartmentalization (PMID: 28525758)
biological.summary: Auxin-inducible degron depletion of CTCF in mouse ES cells showed that CTCF is required, in a dose-dependent manner, for CTCF-site looping and TAD insulation, including in non-dividing cells. A/B compartments stayed segregated after depletion. CTCF acts as an enhancer blocker but not as a direct barrier to heterochromatin spreading.

biological.citation: G-quadruplexes associated with R-loops promote CTCF binding (PMID: 37552993)
biological.summary: R-loops and G-quadruplexes co-localize with CTCF in mouse ES cells and promote CTCF binding to its motif in vitro. R-loop attenuation reduces CTCF binding in vivo, deleting a G4 motif reduces CTCF binding and alters gene expression, and G4 stabilization increases CTCF binding and alters chromatin organization.

biological.citation: CTCF directly binds G-quadruplex structures to regulate genome topology and gene expression (PMID: 42201978)
biological.summary: A proteomics screen identified CTCF as one of the strongest G4 binders, and biochemical work identified a CTCF mutant that prefers G4s over its consensus dsDNA motif. In mESCs reconstituted with this mutant, G4-linked loops were stronger, persistent, and less sensitive to CTCF depletion.

biological.citation: Flavahan et al. 2016 - Insulator dysfunction and oncogene activation in IDH mutant gliomas (PMID: 26700815)
biological.summary: IDH mutant gliomas show hypermethylation at CTCF/cohesin sites, which reduces methylation-sensitive CTCF binding. This causes loss of domain insulation and lets an enhancer contact PDGFRA. CRISPR disruption of the CTCF motif in IDH wild-type gliomaspheres upregulates PDGFRA and increases proliferation, while demethylating treatment partly restores insulation.

biological.citation: T cell-intrinsic cGAS-CTCF regulation maintains regulatory T cell development and function (PMID: 40966077)
biological.summary: Nuclear cGAS in Treg cells recruits CTCF to the Tnfrsf9 (4-1BB) and Tnfrsf4 (OX40) loci through chromatin interactions, sustaining their expression and TCR signaling. This cGAS-CTCF axis acts independently of STING, and Treg-specific cGAS deletion impairs tumor growth in mice.

biological.citation: CTCF-Mediated and Pax6-Associated Gene Expression in Corneal Epithelial Cell-Specific Differentiation (PMID: 27583466)
biological.summary: CTCF expression falls and PAX6 rises during corneal epithelial differentiation. CTCF-mediated chromatin remodeling controls PAX6 interaction with RCN1 and ADAM17 (shown by 4C, ChIP-on-chip and FISH). CTCF shRNA knockdown weakened these interactions and caused earlier onset of the differentiation genes.

biological.citation: CTCF Expression is Essential for Somatic Cell Viability and Protection Against Cancer (PMID: 30513694)
biological.summary: CTCF knockdown or CRISPR editing in K562 cells reduced growth and colony formation and induced cell cycle arrest. In p53-shRNA Ctcf+/- MEFs, haploinsufficiency increased proliferation, supporting CTCF as a haploinsufficient tumour suppressor. Endometrial cancers with CTCF mutations show locus-specific gene dysregulation.

biological.citation: CTCF loss induces giant lamellar bodies in Purkinje cell dendrites (PMID: 36447271)
biological.summary: CTCF is highly expressed in mature cerebellar Purkinje cells compared with other cerebellar neurons. Conditional deletion in mouse PCs caused progressive motor dysfunction, dendritic self-avoidance defects, giant lamellar bodies, mitochondrial swelling and eventual PC loss.

biological.citation: Acute depletion of CTCF rewires genome-wide chromatin accessibility (PMID: 34429148)
biological.summary: Acute auxin-induced degradation of endogenous CTCF rewired chromatin accessibility. Gains in accessibility were found near CTCF sites at promoters and insulators and were associated with increased transcription of nearby genes. A multi-omics pipeline identified 40 candidate CTCF co-regulatory partners.

biological.citation: RNA-binding proteins mediate the maturation of chromatin topology during differentiation (PMID: 40921733)
biological.summary: CTCF-RBP interactions increase on ES-to-neural stem cell differentiation, and the ncRNA Pantr1 facilitates them to reinforce CTCF-anchored topology. Acute CTCF degradation showed that CTCF maintains neuronal gene silencing in NS cells by acting as a barrier to premature gene activation.
